sources: Leningrad Oblast Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko (Telegram, via TASS) + NASA FIRMS + Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova+, via Ukrainska Pravda / Kyiv Independent / Kyiv Post / Al Jazeera

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the strike and the fire] Overnight Nov 10-11, drones struck the port area of Ust-Luga (Kingisepp district, Leningrad Oblast, Baltic Sea), causing a fire at the oil terminal and the emergency shutdown of a transformer substation. Governor Drozdenko confirmed the strikes on the port area and the fire; 3 port workers were injured. NASA FIRMS detected fire hotspots at the port and in adjacent waters. Exilenova+ published footage of explosions and a large fire. Pulkovo (St Petersburg), Pskov and Izhevsk airports had temporary restrictions; two St Petersburg-bound aircraft diverted to Helsinki. [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- the interception tally, running not final] Drozdenko's claimed shootdowns rose through the night: 42, then 92, then 146 (TASS, Nov 10), then 150 overnight (Kyiv Post/Kyiv Independent). Treat as a running official tally, NOT a verified final count; Reuters could not independently confirm. [CONTEXT -- why it matters] Ust-Luga is one of Russia's largest Baltic oil/products export ports, the terminus of Baltic Pipeline System-2, EU/UK/US/Canada/Switzerland-sanctioned, and a shadow-fleet loading point. Second energy site hit in the Leningrad region in 3 days (Kirishi refinery, Russia's second-largest, struck Monday Nov 9, fire + 1 woman killed). Ukraine's Defence Intelligence confirmed a strike on the Novatek-Ust-Luga complex on Sep 1 -- this Nov 11 strike is NOT confirmed by Kyiv as its operation; attribution rests on monitoring channels. [DO NOT CONFLATE] The Baltic shelter alerts of Tuesday night (NATO jets scrambled, no drone found) were recorded at 0800-03 and are a SEPARATE event; the Wednesday-morning Latvia Ludza/Rezekne threat is also in 0800-03.
sections.what_verified: 5 distinct tiered families: Reuters (T1, via AJ -- Ust-Luga fire, 3 injured, refinery context), Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA, own article), Kyiv Independent (T2), TASS (T3, STATE RU, governor's figures), Ukrainska Pravda (T3). Kyiv Post and Militarnyi carry the same facts but have NO declared tier and do not count.
sections.what_disputed: The 146/150 interception figures come only from Governor Drozdenko and cannot be independently verified; they changed repeatedly through the night (42/92/146/150). The precise facilities struck, the damage extent and any interruption to oil-loading are unestablished. No Ukrainian official claim of responsibility for this specific strike has been published; the Sep 1 DIU confirmation covers a different strike. Russian MoD claimed 627 drones intercepted nationwide overnight -- also single-source, unverified.
sections.why_matters: While the world watched Abu Dhabi, drones set fire to Russia's biggest Baltic oil port -- 150 claimed shot down, and the governor still confirmed the fire.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Ukrainska Pravda 2026-11-11T00:58+02:00 = 02:58 ; Kyiv Independent 00:59Z; AJ piece published 04:34Z, updated 07:55Z = 11:55 ; never a standalone item -- only the 92-drone figure appeared in 0800-05 triage) -- Ukrainian drones hit the Ust-Luga oil terminal, Baltic port on fire; 3 workers injured

totw_analysis: Our read: While the world watched Abu Dhabi, drones set fire to Russia's biggest Baltic oil port -- 150 claimed shot down, and the governor still confirmed the fire. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Deep strikes on Russia's export economy: legitimate war-economy target, or escalation onto NATO's Baltic shore?
